faq.a: Haniah is associated with the Arabic form هنية, whose core sense is pleasant, sweet, delightful.

faq.q: What is the origin of Haniah?
faq.a: Haniah is associated with Arabic. Haniah is a transliteration of Arabic هَنِيَّة (Haniyya) 'pleasant, agreeable (feminine)', from the root ه ن أ (h-n-ʾ). The source gloss 'graceful, beautiful, pleasing' is a loose rendering. Same name as hania and haniya.
Yes — the underlying form هنية is Arabic.
Haniah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Haniah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. False

faq.q: What does Haniah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Haniah is rendered ہنیہ and carries the sense خوشگوار، شیریں.

faq.q: What does Haniah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Haniah is rendered هنیه and carries the sense دلپذیر، شیرین.
A romanized syllable approximation is ha-niah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Haniah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Haniah, haniah. Script forms are هنية, هنیه, ہنیہ, हानिया.

faq.q: Is Haniah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
